answers.answer: ripgrep provides rg, a command-line regex search utility that recursively searches files while respecting ignore rules, plus reusable Rust search libraries. Shell users/scripts run rg; Rust applications can depend on the grep facade. The integration harness also launches rg. External downstream applications were not surveyed.

The core binary parses options and orchestrates traversal/search. ignore handles filtered directory walking; globset handles glob matching. grep is the facade. grep-matcher defines the matching interface; grep-regex and optional grep-pcre2 implement it. grep-searcher reads input, finds lines and invokes sinks; grep-printer formats results. grep-cli supplies CLI helpers. grep-index is an optional experimental indexing package.

Primarily Rust, organized as a Cargo workspace with root package ripgrep and ten internal crates (globset, grep, cli, index, matcher, pcre2, printer, regex, searcher, ignore). Root declares rg at crates/core/main.rs, an integration-test target, build.rs, Rust edition 2024 and rust-version 1.96. PCRE2 and unstable indexing are feature-gated. The map also identifies supporting shell scripts and a Ruby Homebrew formula; it reports these languages as analysis limitations, not fully resolved call graphs.

Cargo's rg binary target begins at crates/core/main.rs::main (44-67), which evaluates flags::parse() and passes its result to run (78-107). Parsing starts in flags/parse.rs::parse, then parse_low and HiArgs::from_low_args.

Sequential orchestration is the root ripgrep binary's search function in crates/core/main.rs:113-157. Per-file dispatch is SearchWorker<W>::search (core/search.rs:245-267), then its search_path and the generic search_path helper. Actual file reading/search belongs to grep-searcher::Searcher::search_path (searcher/mod.rs:643-657).

grep directly depends on grep-cli, grep-matcher, grep-printer, grep-regex and grep-searcher, plus optional grep-pcre2. Each direction grep → package is declared by a relative path dependency in crates/grep/Cargo.toml and confirmed by public extern-crate reexports as cli, matcher, printer, regex, searcher and feature-gated pcre2 in lib.rs. ignore, globset and grep-index are not direct dependencies of this facade.

Assuming valid PATTERN, readable FILE and no configuration altering the requested mode: main → flags::parse → parse_low → HiArgs::from_low_args → run → sequential search (threads == 1; indexing bypassed). A single-file input also forces one thread. WalkBuilder.build yields a Haystack; search constructs matcher/searcher/printer and calls SearchWorker.search. Ordinary-file dispatch selects worker.search_path → generic search_path → Standard sink → grep-searcher Searcher.search_path → File::open → search_file_maybe_path. Successful mmap uses search_slice/SliceByLine; otherwise ordinary line search uses search_reader/ReadByLine. Sink.has_match becomes SearchResult, aggregated into matched: exit 0 for a match, 1 for none, 2 for errors, with explicit broken-pipe handling. Runtime boundaries include configuration, I/O, mmap availability, encoding, pattern compilation and terminal-dependent output; the map is not an execution trace.

Two direct production consumers are evidenced in pinned source: main.rs::search's per-haystack loop and main.rs::search_parallel's walker callback. Both construct SearchWorker and call search(&haystack). A signature/contract change therefore requires checking both; whether behavior changes depends on the edit. The optional index reader delegates to these outer functions, so it is indirect. Lattice exact-call lookup returned zero incoming edges: that omission does not establish absence of callers.

The r99 integration regression creates foo1/bar with matching text and foo2 without, invokes -j1 --heading test, and asserts output. TestCommand launches the rg binary, entering main/run/sequential search; its harness removes RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH. The simplegrep example independently loops ordinary files and calls Searcher.search_path with RegexMatcher and a Standard printer sink; it exercises the library without SearchWorker. These are inspected source examples/tests, not tests executed in this trial.

flags/config.rs::args reads std::env::var_os("RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH"); missing/empty means no arguments, otherwise it becomes PathBuf. parse opens the file; parse_reader trims byte lines, ignores blank/comment lines, and converts each remaining whole line into one OsString argument (no shell token splitting). Read/conversion errors are reported. parse_low first parses CLI options, bypasses config for special help/version modes or --no-config, then prepends config arguments to CLI arguments and reparses LowArgs, resetting message/log levels before HiArgs conversion.
